title: Evaluation of ocular surface inflammation in different forms of dry eye disease using HRT III in comparison with clinical parameters
summary: The non-invasive examination of the cornea using confocal in vivo microscopy (IVCM) and the subsequent evaluation of activated dendritic cells can contribute to the early detection of ocular surface inflammation in patients with dry eye and may lead to improved treatment recommendations in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Dry eye requiring treatment:
OSDI score ≥ 13 and additionally
1. either non-invasive tear film break-up time (NIBUT) < 10 seconds and/or
2. ocular surface stippling > 5 corneal spots (Oxford scale ≥ 1) + a low Schirmer I test of ≤ 5 mm)
Subclassification:
Patients are classified as evaporative dry eye (EDE group) if they have a NIBUT of < 10 seconds and a Schirmer I test of > 5 mm.
Patients are classified as hypovolaemic dry eye (ADDE group) if they have a low Schirmer I test of ≤ 5 mm.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who would not be able to attend the follow-up appointments due to other illnesses or who cannot give their consent to the study are excluded.
Furthermore, corneal surgery, inflammatory eye diseases (e.g. uveitis), tumour diseases and treatment with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive medication in the last 3 months are exclusion criteria.
